mishnayot.hebrewFull: הַנּוֹטֵעַ לִסְיָג וּלְקוֹרוֹת, פָּטוּר מִן הָעָרְלָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אָמַר הַפְּנִימִי לְמַאֲכָל וְהַחִיצוֹן לִסְיָג, הַפְּנִימִי חַיָּב, וְהַחִיצוֹן פָּטוּר:
mishnayot.englishFull: One who plants [a fruit tree] as a fence or to provide wood beams, it is exempt from [the law of] orlah. Rabbi Yose says: even if he said “The inward [facing part of the tree] is for food, and the outward [facing part] is for a fence,” the inward [facing part] is subject [to orlah], and the outward [facing part] is exempt.

grammar.notes: Mishnaic term meaning exempt from obligation.
Refers to the forbidden first three years of fruit.

grammar.pos: Verb, past tense, 3rd person masculine singular

grammar.notes: Mishnaic term meaning obligated / bound by the law.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: עֵת שֶׁבָּאוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לָאָרֶץ, מָצְאוּ נָטוּעַ, פָּטוּר. נָטְעוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כִבְּשׁוּ, חַיָּב. הַנּוֹטֵעַ לָרַבִּים, חַיָּב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר. הַנּוֹטֵעַ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְהַנָּכְרִי שֶׁנָּטַע, וְהַגַּזְלָן שֶׁנָּטַע, וְהַנּוֹטֵעַ בִּסְפִינָה, וְהָעוֹלֶה מֵאֵלָיו, חַיָּב בָּעָרְלָה:
mishnayot.englishFull: If at the time when our ancestors came into the land and they found [a tree already] planted it was exempt [from the laws of orlah]. If they planted [a tree], even though they had not yet conquered [the land], it was subject [to orlah]. If one planted a tree for [the use of] the many, it is subject. But Rabbi Judah makes it exempt. If one has planted [a tree] in the public domain, or if a non-Jew has planted, or if a robber has planted, or one who plants on a boat, or [a tree] that has grown of itself, it is subject to orlah.

grammar.notes: Mishnaic technical term for exempt from a commandment.
Part of the compound idiom 'af al pi she-' (even though).
Refers to the prohibition of the fruit of trees during their first three years.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: אִילָן שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר וְהַסֶּלַע עִמּוֹ, שְׁטָפוֹ נָהָר וְהַסֶּלַע עִמּוֹ, אִם יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת, פָּטוּר, וְאִם לָאו, חַיָּב. נֶעֱקַר הַסֶּלַע מִצִּדּוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁזִּעְזְעַתּוּ הַמַּחֲרֵשָׁה, אוֹ שֶׁזִּעְזְעוֹ וַעֲשָׂאוֹ כְעָפָר, אִם יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת, פָּטוּר, וְאִם לָאו, חַיָּב:
mishnayot.englishFull: If a tree was uprooted and the hard soil together with it, or if a stream swept it away and the hard soil together with it, [then] if it could have lived it is exempt, But if [it could] not, it is subject. If the hard soil has been detached from its side, or if a ploughshare shook it, or if someone shook it, and one reset it with earth, [then] if it could have lived, it is exempt, But if not, it is subject.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: אִילָן שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ, פָּטוּר. וְכַמָּה יְהֵא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ בַּרְתּוֹתָא, כְּמַחַט שֶׁל מִתּוּן:
mishnayot.englishFull: If a tree was uprooted and one root was left [in the ground], it is exempt. How much must the [thickness of the] root be? Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel said in the name of Rabb Eliezer ben Judah a man of Bartota: as [thick as] a pin [used for] stretching.

grammar.notes: Mishnaic term for exemption from Orlah
Refers to a weaver's tool used for stretching

mishnayot.hebrewFull: אִילָן שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר וּבוֹ בְרֵכָה, וְהוּא חָיֶּה מִמֶּנָּה, חָזְרָה הַזְּקֵנָה לִהְיוֹת כַּבְּרֵכָה. הִבְרִיכָהּ שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה, וְנִפְסְקָה, מוֹנֶה מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה. סִפּוּק הַגְּפָנִים, וְסִפּוּק עַל גַּבֵּי סִפּוּק, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִבְרִיכָן בָּאָרֶץ, מֻתָּר. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, מָקוֹם שֶׁכֹּחָהּ יָפֶה, מֻתָּר, וְמָקוֹם שֶׁכֹּחָהּ רָע, אָסוּר. וְכֵן בְּרֵכָה שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה וְהִיא מְלֵאָה פֵרוֹת, אִם הוֹסִיף בְּמָאתַיִם, אָסוּר:
mishnayot.englishFull: A tree which was uprooted and it has a bent-down [and rooted] shoot, and it [the tree] derives sustenance from it [the shoot], the old [tree] is [considered] like the shoot. If one bends [and roots] from it year after year, and it became detached, one counts from the time it became detached. A grafted shoot of vines, and a grafted shoot [growing] on another grafted shoot, even if he rooted them in the soil, they are permitted. Rabbi Meir said: in an instance where it is strongly [grafted], it is permitted, but in an instance where it is poorly [grafted], it is prohibited. A bent-down [and rooted] shoot that has become detached and is full of fruit, [then] if it increased one two hundredth, it is prohibited.

grammar.notes: A vine or tree branch bent down into the earth to root
Refers to the original uprooted tree
Part of idiom af al pi she-
Refers to the ratio of 1 in 200 for nullification in Orlah

mishnayot.hebrewFull: נְטִיעָה שֶׁל עָרְלָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בִנְטִיעוֹת, הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִלְקֹט. וְאִם לָקַט, יַעֲלֶה בְאֶחָד וּמָאתַיִם, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּן לִלְקֹט. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף יִתְכַּוֵּן לִלְקֹט וְיַעֲלֶה בְאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: If a shoot of orlah or a vineyard in which seeds had been planted (kilayim), became mixed up with [other] shoots, behold one may not gather [the fruit]. But if one has gathered [it], it is neutralized in two hundred-and-one, provided that he did not act deliberately. Rabbi Yose says: even if he acted deliberately, it becomes neutralized in two hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: first three years of fruit tree growth
halakhic term for annulment in a mixture

mishnayot.hebrewFull: הֶעָלִים, וְהַלּוּלָבִים, וּמֵי גְּפָנִים, וּסְמָדַר, מֻתָּרִים בָּעָרְלָה וּבָרְבָעִי וּבַנָּזִיר, וַאֲסוּרִים בָּאֲשֵׁרָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַסְּמָדַר אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פְּרִי. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַמַּעֲמִיד בִּשְׂרָף הָעָרְלָה, אָסוּר. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּפֵרוּשׁ, שֶׁהַמַּעֲמִיד בִּשְׂרָף הֶעָלִים וּבִשְׂרָף הָעִקָּרִים, מֻתָּר, בִּשְׂרָף הַפַּגִּים, אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם פְּרִי:
mishnayot.englishFull: Leaves, sprouts, sap of vines, and vine-buds are permitted in respect of orlah and the laws of the fourth year, and to a nazirite, but are prohibited if they come from an Asherah [tree]. Rabbi Yose says: vine-buds are prohibited because they are fruit. Rabbi Eliezer said: if one curdles [milk] with the resinous substances of [a tree liable to] orlah, it is prohibited. Rabbi Joshua said: I have received an explicit tradition that if one curdles [milk] with the resinous substance of the leaves, or with the resinous substance of the roots, it is permitted, but with the resinous substance of the unripe berries, it is prohibited, because these are fruit.

grammar.notes: Refers here to tender shoots or fronds
Prohibited fruit of young trees in first three years
Neta Revai - fruit of fourth year eaten in Jerusalem
Idolatrous tree whose benefit is forbidden forever
Hifil participle, causing milk to curdle/set

mishnayot.hebrewFull: עַנְקוֹקְלוֹת, וְהַחַרְצַנִּים, וְהַזַּגִּים, וְהַתֶּמֶד שֶׁלָּהֶם, קְלִפֵּי רִמּוֹן וְהַנֵּץ שֶׁלּוֹ, קְלִפֵּי אֱגוֹזִים, וְהַגַּרְעִינִים, אֲסוּרִים בָּעָרְלָה, וּבָאֲשֵׁרָה, וּבַנָּזִיר, וּמֻתָּרִין בָּרְבָעִי. וְהַנּוֹבְלוֹת, כֻּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת:
mishnayot.englishFull: Defective grapes, grape kernels, grape husks, and the temed drink made from them, the peel of a pomegranate and its sprout, nutshells, and fruit-seeds, are all subject to the laws of orlah, asherah and a nazirite, but permitted in respect of a fourth year vineyard. Fallen unripe fruit is subject to all of them.

grammar.notes: Mishnaic term for shriveled or defective grapes.
Prefixed with conjunction and definite article.
Prefixed with conjunction and definite article.
A weak wine made by soaking grape skins and seeds in water.
Prefixed with conjunction and definite article.
Possessive suffix attached to prepositional construct.
Prefixed with conjunction and definite article.
Refers to the prohibition of fruit in its first three years.
Refers to a tree worshipped as an idol.
Refers to the restrictions of a nazirite regarding grape products.
Masculine plural predicate indicating legal permissibility.
Refers to ma'aser sheni of the fourth year.
Refers to fruit that fell off the tree prematurely while unripe.
Femininely suffixed pronoun referring to the novlot.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, נוֹטְעִין יִחוּר שֶׁל עָרְלָה, וְאֵין נוֹטְעִין אֱגוֹז שֶׁל עָרְלָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פְּרִי. וְאֵין מַרְכִּיבִין בְּכַפְנִיּוֹת שֶׁל עָרְלָה:
mishnayot.englishFull: Rabbi Yose says: one may plant a shoot of orlah; But one may not plant a nut of orlah, because it is fruit. And one may not graft early date berries of orlah.

grammar.notes: Mishnaic plural used as general third-person
Refers to forbidden first three years of fruit growth

mishnayot.hebrewFull: הַתְּרוּמָה, וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁל דְּמַאי, הַחַלָּה וְהַבִּכּוּרִים, עוֹלִים בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, וְצָרִיךְ לְהָרִים. הָעָרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, עוֹלִים בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתַיִם, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָרִים. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מִצְטָרְפִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, אֲבָל לֹא לֶאֱסֹר:
mishnayot.englishFull: Terumah, terumat maaser of demai, hallah and bikkurim, are neutralized in a hundred-and-one mixture. And they are reckoned together [to form the statutory minimum]. And it is necessary to remove [from the mixture an amount equal to that of the consecrated produce contained in it]. Orlah and kilayim of the vineyard are neutralized in a two-hundred-and-one mixture. And they are reckoned together [to form the statutory minimum]. But it is not necessary to remove [from the mixture an amount equal to that of the consecrated produce contained in it]. Rabbi Shimon says: they are not reckoned together. Rabbi Eliezer says: they are reckoned together when they impart flavor, but not to prohibit.

grammar.notes: Produce whose tithing status is doubtful
Portion of dough given to the priest
Literally 'go up', meaning they are nullified in a mixture
Combined to reach the minimum quantity
Separating out an equivalent amount of consecrated produce
Fruit of trees in their first three years

mishnayot.hebrewFull: הַתְּרוּמָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה, וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה. כֵּיצַד, סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפְלוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה קַבִּין עָרְלָה, אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה קַבִּין כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, זוֹ הִיא שֶׁהַתְּרוּמָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה:
mishnayot.englishFull: Terumah can void orlah, and orlah can void terumah. How so? [For instance] a seah of terumah fell into one hundred, and afterwards three kavs of orlah or three kavs of mixed-seeds of the vineyard [fell in]. This is [an instance] where terumah goes towards neutralizing orlah, and orlah terumah.

grammar.notes: Mishnaic idiom for neutralizing forbidden mixtures

mishnayot.hebrewFull: הָעָרְלָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הַכִּלְאַיִם, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם אֶת הָעָרְלָה, וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה. כֵּיצַד, סְאָה עָרְלָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמָאתַיִם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפְלָה סְאָה וְעוֹד עָרְלָה, אוֹ סְאָה וְעוֹד שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, זוֹ הִיא שֶׁהָעָרְלָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הַכִּלְאַיִם, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם אֶת הָעָרְלָה, וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה:
mishnayot.englishFull: Orlah can void kilayim, and kilayim [can void] orlah, and orlah [can void] orlah. How so? A seah of orlah falls into two hundred [seahs] and afterwards there falls in a seah and a little bit more of orlah, or a seah and a little bit more of kilayim of the vineyard--this is [a case] where orlah can void kilayim, and kilayim [can void] orlah, and orlah [can void] orlah.

grammar.shoreshMeaning: uncircumcised / forbidden fruit of young trees
to go up / neutralize / nullify in mixture

mishnayot.hebrewFull: כָּל הַמְחַמֵּץ וְהַמְתַבֵּל וְהַמְדַמֵּעַ בַּתְּרוּמָה וּבָעָרְלָה וּבְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, אָסוּר. וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אַף מְטַמֵּא. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כַּבֵּיצָה:
mishnayot.englishFull: Whatever causes something to ferment, or seasons, or makes medumma with terumah, with orlah or with ‘mixed-seeds’ of the vineyard, is prohibited. Bet Shammai says: it also renders unclean. But Bet Hillel says: it never renders unclean unless it has the volume of an egg.

grammar.notes: Generalizing term at the start of the clause.
Hiphil/Piel participle referring to a substance that causes fermentation.
Fruits of a tree in its first three years.
Kil'ei hakerm - mixed seeds of the vineyard.
Present tense plural used for quoting opinions.
Literally 'for eternity', idiomatically 'never' when combined with negative.
He is not / it is not.

grammar.pos: relative particle + qal imperfect 3rd person masculine singular

mishnayot.hebrewFull: דּוֹסְתַּאי אִישׁ כְּפַר יִתְמָה, הָיָה מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי, וְאָמַר, שָׁמַעְתִּי מִשַּׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן שֶׁאָמַר, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כַּבֵּיצָה:
mishnayot.englishFull: Dostai of Kefar Yitmah was one of the disciples of Bet Shammai, and he said, “I received a tradition from Shammai the elder who said: “It never renders unclean unless it contains the volume of an egg.”

grammar.notes: Used in rabbinic literature for receiving a received tradition
In rabbinic Hebrew, 'le-olam' often means 'ever' or with negation 'never'
Piel conjugation indicates causative action (to make ritually impure)
Here part of the idiom 'ad she-' (until that / unless)

mishnayot.hebrewFull: וּלְמָה אָמְרוּ כָּל הַמְחַמֵּץ וְהַמְתַבֵּל וְהַמְדַמֵּעַ לְהַחֲמִיר, מִין בְּמִינוֹ. לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ. כֵּיצַד, שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חִטִּים שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ עִסַּת חִטִּים, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, אָסוּר. אֵין בּוֹ לַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, בֵּין שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, אָסוּר:
mishnayot.englishFull: Concerning what did they say: “Anything that causes fermentation or seasons or which renders medumma we rule stringently”? [In the case of] a species [mixed] with its [like] species. [When did they say] “we rule [sometimes] leniently and [sometimes] stringently”? [In the case of] a species [mixed] with a different kind of species. How so? If leaven of wheat fell into dough of wheat and there is enough to cause fermentation, [then] whether there is enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, or there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, it is prohibited. If there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, [then] whether there is enough to cause fermentation, or there is not enough to cause fermentation, it is prohibited.

grammar.notes: Medumma refers to unconsecrated produce mixed with terumah.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, כֵּיצַד. כְּגוֹן גְּרִיסִין שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם עֲדָשִׁים, וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, אָסוּר. אֵין בָּהֶם בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, מֻתָּר:
mishnayot.englishFull: [We rule sometimes] leniently and [sometimes] stringently, [in the case of] a species [mixed] with a different kind of species. How so? If crushed beans were boiled together with lentils, and there is enough of them [the crushed beans] to impart flavor, [then] whether there is enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, or there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, it is prohibited. [But] if there is not enough to impart flavor, [then] whether there is enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, or there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, [the mixture] is permitted.

grammar.notes: Halakhic term for nullification (being negated in a mixture)

mishnayot.hebrewFull: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפַל שְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אוֹ שְׂאֹר שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, אָסוּר:
mishnayot.englishFull: If leaven of hullin has fallen into dough, and there was enough of it to cause fermentation, and after that leaven of terumah fell in or leaven of kilayim of the vineyard, and there is enough to cause fermentation, [the dough] is prohibited.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה וְחִמְּצָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפַל שְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה אוֹ שְׂאֹר שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, אָסוּר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר:
mishnayot.englishFull: If leaven of hullin has fallen into dough and caused it to ferment, and after that there fell in leaven of terumah or of kilayim of the vineyard, and there was enough to cause fermentation, [the dough] is prohibited. But Rabbi Shimon permits it.

grammar.notes: hullin refers to ordinary, non-sacred (non-terumah) produce
Piel conjugation with 3rd fem. sing. object suffix
priestly portion set aside from produce
Hifil participle, halakhic term for permitting

mishnayot.hebrewFull: תְּבָלִין, שְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת מִמִּין אֶחָד, אוֹ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה, אָסוּר, וּמִצְטָרְפִין. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת מִמִּין אֶחָד, אוֹ שְׁנֵי מִינִין מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין:
mishnayot.englishFull: Seasonings [consisting] of two or three categories of one species, or [consisting] of three species [of one category], are forbidden and combine. Rabbi Shimon said: Two or three categories of one species, or two species of one category, do not combine.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חֻלִּין וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, לֹא בָּזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ וְלֹא בָּזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, נִצְטָרְפוּ וְחִמְּצוּ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַחַר הָאַחֲרוֹן אֲנִי בָא. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין שֶׁנָּפַל אִסּוּר בַּתְּחִלָּה, בֵּין בַּסּוֹף, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ:
mishnayot.englishFull: Leaven of hullin and of terumah fell into dough, and neither this was sufficient to cause fermentation nor was that sufficient to cause fermentation, but together they caused [the dough] to ferment:Rabbi Eliezer says: I go after the last. But the sages say: whether the prohibited fell in first or last, it never causes the dough to become prohibited unless there is enough to cause fermentation.

grammar.notes: Heave-offering set aside for the priest

mishnayot.hebrewFull: יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ הַבִּירָה הָיָה מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְאָמַר, שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן עוֹמֵד בְּשַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח, וְאָמַר, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ:
mishnayot.englishFull: Yoezer, master of the temple (Ish Habirah), was one of the disciples of Bet Shammai and he said: I asked Rabban Gamaliel the elder as he was standing at the eastern gate [of the Temple], and he said: it never causes the dough to become prohibited unless there is enough to cause fermentation.

grammar.notes: Refers to the Temple mount area
Present participle used as finite verb

mishnayot.hebrewFull: כֵּלִים שֶׁסָּכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָמֵא, וְחָזַר וְסָכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָהוֹר, אוֹ שֶׁסָּכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָהוֹר, וְחָזַר וְסָכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָמֵא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַחַר הָרִאשׁוֹן אֲנִי בָּא. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַחַר הָאַחֲרוֹן:
mishnayot.englishFull: Vessels which were oiled with unclean oil, and [later] he returned and oiled them with clean oil; Or he [first] oiled them with clean oil, and [later] he returned [to them] and oiled them with unclean oil: Rabbi Eliezer says: “I go after the first.” And the sages say: after the last.

conjunction + verb, Qal, past, 3rd person masculine singular
grammar.notes: Used in Mishnaic Hebrew to mean doing an action again.

grammar.pos: conjunction + verb, Qal, past, 3rd person masculine singular + suffix
relative particle + verb, Qal, past, 3rd person masculine singular + suffix
conjunction + verb, Qal, past, 3rd person masculine singular
conjunction + verb, Qal, past, 3rd person masculine singular + suffix

grammar.notes: Idiomatic usage: 'I come after' means 'I follow the rule of'.

grammar.pos: conjunction + definite article + noun, masculine plural

mishnayot.hebrewFull: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, לֹא בָזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ וְלֹא בָזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, וְנִצְטָרְפוּ וְחִמְּצוּ, אָסוּר לְזָרִים וּמֻתָּר לַכֹּהֲנִים. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר לְזָרִים וְלַכֹּהֲנִים:
mishnayot.englishFull: Leaven of terumah and of kilayim of the vineyard which fell into dough, this one is not sufficient to cause fermentation, nor is that one sufficient to cause fermentation, but together they cause fermentation:It [the dough] is prohibited to non-priests and permitted to priests. Rabbi Shimon permits it to both to non-priests and to priests.

grammar.notes: heave-offering set aside for the priest

words.shoresh: ע - ס - ס / ע - ס - ה
פ - ט - ר / מ - ת - ר

mishnayot.hebrewFull: תְּבָלִין שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁנָּפְלוּ בַּקְּדֵרָה, לֹא בָאֵלוּ כְדֵי לְתַבֵּל וְלֹא בָאֵלּוּ כְדֵי לְתַבֵּל, וְנִצְטָרְפוּ וְתִבְּלוּ, אָסוּר לְזָרִים וּמֻתָּר לַכֹּהֲנִים. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר לְזָרִים וְלַכֹּהֲנִים:
mishnayot.englishFull: Seasonings of terumah and of kilayim of the vineyard that fell into a dish, and there is not enough of one to season, nor is there of the other to season, but together they seasoned:It [the dish] is prohibited to non-priests but permitted to priests. Rabbi Shimon declares it permitted to non-priests and to priests.

grammar.notes: Prohibited mixtures (specifically in a vineyard here)
Prefix preposition + plural noun + definite article
Conjunction + preposition + plural noun + definite article

mishnayot.hebrewFull: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים, שֶׁל פִּגּוּל, וְשֶׁל נוֹתָר, שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם הַחֲתִיכוֹת, אָסוּר לְזָרִים וּמֻתָּר לַכֹּהֲנִים. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר לְזָרִים וְלַכֹּהֲנִים:
mishnayot.englishFull: A piece of [meat from] one of the most holy [sacrifices] and [a piece] of [meat which is] piggul, or remnant, which were cooked with other pieces, it [the non-sacred meat] is prohibited to non-priests but permitted to priests. Rabbi Shimon declares it permitted to non-priests and to priests.

grammar.notes: Refers to offerings of the highest degree of sanctity (kodshei kodashim).
An offering disqualified by improper intent.
Sacrificial meat left past its permitted time.

grammar.pos: relative particle + verb, Nitpa'el, masculine plural

grammar.notes: Zar here means a non-priest unauthorized to eat sacrificial food.

grammar.pos: preposition + definite article + noun, masculine plural
conjunction + preposition + definite article + noun, plural

mishnayot.hebrewFull: בְּשַׂר קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וּבְשַׂר קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם בְּשַׂר הַתַּאֲוָה, אָסוּר לִטְמֵאִים וּמֻתָּר לִטְהוֹרִים:
mishnayot.englishFull: Meat of most holy [sacrifices] and meat of less holy [sacrifices] were cooked together with ordinary meat: [the dish] is prohibited to the unclean, but permitted to the clean.

grammar.notes: Refers to sacrifices of the highest degree of sanctity (קדשי קדשים).
Refers to lesser-degree holy offerings (קדשים קלים).

grammar.pos: relative prefix + verb, Hitpa'el, past, 3rd plural
grammar.notes: Hitpa'el stem denotes reflexive/passive cooking action.
Literally 'desire', here denoting unconsecrated meat slaughtered for consumption rather than sacrifice (ordinary meat).
Standard Mishnaic legal term for forbidden.
Standard Mishnaic legal term for permitted.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: בֶּגֶד שֶׁצְּבָעוֹ בִקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה, יִדָּלֵק. נִתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים, כֻּלָּם יִדָּלֵקוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלֶה בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: A garment dyed with peels of orlah [fruit] must be burned. If it became mixed up with other [garments], all of them shall be burned, the words of Rabbi Meir. But the sages say: it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: Prefix she- (that) + Piel verb + object suffix

grammar.shoreshMeaning: uncircumcised, forbidden fruit of young trees
grammar.notes: Refers to forbidden produce of trees in their first three years
Nif'al future/imperfect, third person masculine singular

grammar.shoreshMeaning: to go up, ascend, be added/neutralized
grammar.notes: Halakhic term meaning to be nullified in a mixture
Dual form (200), prefixed with conjunction u-

mishnayot.hebrewFull: הַצּוֹבֵעַ מְלֹא הַסִּיט בִּקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה, וַאֲרָגוֹ בְבֶגֶד, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה הוּא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, יִדָּלֵק הַבֶּגֶד. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלֶה בְאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: If one dyed a thread the whole [length] of a sit with orlah peels, and wove it into a garment, and it is not known which [thread] it is:Rabbi Meir says: the garment must be burned; But the sages say: it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: A measure equal to half a handbreadth.
Fruit of the first three years of tree growth.

grammar.shoreshMeaning: to go up / be mixed in
grammar.notes: Halakhic term for nullification in a mixture (batel).
Refers to the ratio of two hundred parts of permitted material to one part of forbidden material (plus the one forbidden thread itself).

mishnayot.hebrewFull: הָאוֹרֵג מְלֹא הַסִּיט מִצֶּמֶר הַבְּכוֹר בְּבֶגֶד, יִדָּלֵק הַבֶּגֶד. וּמִשְּׂעַר הַנָּזִיר וּמִפֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר בְּשַׂק, יִדָּלֵק הַשָּׂק. וּבְמֻקְדָּשִׁין, מְקַדְּשִׁין כָּל שֶׁהֵן:
mishnayot.englishFull: If one wove thread the whole [length] of a sit from [the wool of a] first-born animal into a garment, the garment must be burned. [If from] the hair of a nazirite or of the first-born of a donkey into sack-cloth, the sack-cloth must be burned. And if even the smallest amount [from wool or hair of] consecrated [animals], that which it is woven into] is consecrated.

grammar.notes: Qal active participle functioning as conditional 'if one weaves'.
A measurement of length (distance from thumb to index finger).
Mandatory destruction rule for prohibited mixtures.
Refers to 'peter chamor' (first-born of a donkey).
'kol she-hen' translates to 'whatever amount' or 'even the smallest amount'.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: תַּבְשִׁיל שֶׁבִּשְּׁלוֹ בִקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה, יִדָּלֵק. נִתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים, יַעֲלֶה בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: A dish which one cooked with shells of orlah must be burned. If [the dish] became mixed up with other [dishes], it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: Prefix she- means 'that/which', followed by a Qal perfect verb with 3rd person plural/impersonal subject.
Preposition be- ('with/in') attached to the construct plural noun of qlipah (peel/shell).
Refers to the forbidden first three years of fruit growth.
Nifal imperfect, 3rd person masculine singular, used in Mishnah to mandate destruction by fire for prohibited mixtures.
Preposition be- ('with') plus masculine plural adjective/noun.

grammar.shoreshMeaning: to go up / ascend / be nullified in a mixture
grammar.notes: Qal imperfect, 3rd person masculine singular; technical Mishnaic term for nullification (bitul) in a mixture.
Conjunction u- ('and') plus the dual form for two hundred.

mishnayot.hebrewFull: תַּנּוּר שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ בִקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה וְאָפָה בוֹ אֶת הַפַּת, תִּדָּלֵק הַפָּת. נִתְעָרְבָה בַאֲחֵרוֹת, תַּעֲלֶה בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: An oven that was lit with shells of orlah, and then one baked bread in it, the bread must be burned. If it became mixed up with other [loaves] it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: Halakhic term for nullification in a mixture

mishnayot.hebrewFull: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, יִדָּלֵקוּ. נִתְעָרְבוּ בַאֲחֵרִים, כֻּלָּם יִדָּלֵקוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלוּ בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: If one has bundles of fenugreek of kilayim of the vineyard, they must be burned. If they became mixed up with others, all of them must be burned, the words of Rabbi Meir. But the sages say they become neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: Used here in the sense of 'whoever' or 'if one'
Refers to forbidden mixtures in agriculture
Standard term for destruction of forbidden agricultural produce
Refers to the majority rabbinic opinion

grammar.shoreshMeaning: to ascend / go up / become part of
grammar.notes: Halakhic idiom meaning the prohibited substance is nullified in the mixture

mishnayot.hebrewFull: שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִמָּנוֹת, מְקַדֵּשׁ. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶלָּא שִׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים בִּלְבָד. וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, שִׁבְעָה. וְאֵלּוּ הֵם, אֱגוֹזֵי פֶרֶךְ, רִמּוֹנֵי בָדָן, וְחָבִיּוֹת סְתוּמוֹת, וְחֻלְפוֹת תְּרָדִין, וְקֻלְסֵי כְרוּב, וּדְלַעַת יְוָנִית. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אַף כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת. הָרָאוּי לְעָרְלָה, עָרְלָה. לְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, כִּלְאֵי הַכָּרֶם:
mishnayot.englishFull: For Rabbi Meir used to say: anything that is normally [sold] by counting causes [a mixture] to become consecrated [in even the smallest amount]. But the sages say only six things consecrate [a mixture in even the smallest amount], and Rabbi Akiba says seven [things]. And these are they: Nuts with soft shells; badan pomegranates; stopped-up casks; beet shoots; cabbage-heads; Greek pumpkins. Rabbi Akiba says: also loaves [baked by] a householder. To those to which orlah applies [they prohibit the mixture] as orlah, [to those of which] kilayim of the vineyard apply [they prohibit the mixture as] kilayim of the vineyard.

grammar.notes: Prefix she- (that/for) + past tense of 'to be'
Present participle used for ongoing past habit
In Orlah context, makes the mixture forbidden like Orlah in any amount
Elliptical: it prohibits the mixture as orlah
Elliptical conclusion matching the previous clause

mishnayot.hebrewFull: כֵּיצַד. נִתְפַּצְּעוּ הָאֱגוֹזִים, נִתְפָּרְדוּ הָרִמּוֹנִים, נִתְפַּתְּחוּ הֶחָבִיּוֹת, נִתְחַתְּכוּ הַדְּלוּעִים, נִתְפָּרְסוּ הַכִּכָּרוֹת, יַעֲלוּ בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
mishnayot.englishFull: How so? If the nuts cracked, or if the pomegranates burst open, or the casks became unstopped, or the pumpkins were cut, or the loaves were broken up, they become neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

grammar.notes: Passive form describing produce breaking open

grammar.shoreshMeaning: to divide or break into slices

grammar.notes: Halakhic idiom meaning the prohibited amount is nullified in the majority

words.shoresh: א - ח - ד / מ - א - ה

grammar.notes: Ratio required for nullification in certain contexts

mishnayot.hebrewFull: סְפֵק עָרְלָה, בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר, וּבְסוּרְיָא מֻתָּר, וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יוֹרֵד וְלוֹקֵחַ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶנּוּ לוֹקֵט. כֶּרֶם נָטוּעַ יָרָק, וְיָרָק נִמְכָּר חוּצָה לוֹ, בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר, וּבְסוּרְיָא מֻתָּר, וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יוֹרֵד וְלוֹקֵט, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִלְקֹט בַּיָּד. הֶחָדָשׁ, אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם. וְהָעָרְלָה, הֲלָכָה. וְהַכִּלְאַיִם, מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים:
mishnayot.englishFull: Doubtful orlah: in the land of Israel is prohibited, in Syria is permitted, and outside the land one may go down and purchase [from a non-Israelite] as long as he has not seen him gathering it. A vineyard planted with vegetables [which are kilayim], and they [the vegetables] are sold outside of it: in the land of Israel these are prohibited, and in Syria they are permitted; outside the land one may go down and purchase them as long as he does not gather [them] with [one’s own] hand. New [produce] is prohibited by the Torah in all places. And orlah is a halachah. And kilayim are an enactment of the scribes.

grammar.notes: Standard Mishnaic term for halakhic prohibition.
Standard Mishnaic term for halakhic permissibility.
Refers to traveling down to the diaspora markets.
Refers to new grain before the Omer offering (Chadash).
Refers to a law received by tradition (Halachah le-Mosheh mi-Sinai).
